headline_marked: [[AMD launches Instella-MoE-16B-A3B]] AI model, trained entirely on its own GPUs, ditching Nvidia
headline: AMD launches Instella-MoE-16B-A3B AI model, trained entirely on its own GPUs, ditching Nvidia
summary: AMD's new 16-billion parameter AI model, Instella-MoE-16B-A3B, was trained end-to-end on AMD Instinct MI300X and MI325X GPUs, showcasing its independent AI training capabilities.
details: AMD has unveiled Instella-MoE-16B-A3B, a new 16-billion parameter AI model. Its key distinction is that it was trained entirely on AMD's own Instinct MI300X and MI325X GPUs, a direct challenge to Nvidia's dominance in AI training.

The model utilizes a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, meaning only 2.8 billion parameters are actively used per token. This design allows for faster processing while maintaining a broad knowledge base.

This release is significant because it proves AMD's hardware can handle top-tier AI training without relying on Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem. This opens up a viable alternative for developers and researchers.

AMD has made the model highly transparent, releasing weights for every training step, the training code, and data recipes. This "open-book" approach allows the community to verify, reproduce, and build upon their work.

Instella-MoE-16B-A3B features a decoder-only MoE design incorporating architectural innovations like Gated Multi-head Latent Attention (Gated MLA) and FarSkip-Collective for efficient communication and computation. It also uses Multi-Token Prediction for improved language learning.

The model is relatively accessible, requiring only about 32GB of VRAM for the 16B BF16 parameters. This means it can run on a single high-end GPU, making it suitable for smaller research teams without expensive GPU clusters.
While the model weights are under a ResearchRAIL license (research-only), the training code is MIT licensed. This dual licensing strategy encourages both academic exploration and broader development.

This move by AMD underscores a larger shift in the AI chip competition: the battle for software ecosystems. By providing open tools and models, AMD aims to build confidence in its ROCm platform and attract developers away from Nvidia's established ecosystem.
